skill.name: bounce-recovery
skill.description: Uses Leadsets to recheck bounced work emails and find updated addresses. It separates verified replacements, catch-all addresses, original addresses that now verify, and unresolved contacts.
skill.summary: Recheck bounced work emails and find verified replacements with Leadsets.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The workflow sends contact data to the documented Leadsets service; Markdown, setup links, and ordinary workflow terms account for the other static alerts. The default bulk workflow lacks a separate transfer approval step, and verified addresses are labeled ready to send without a suppression check. No evidence found of audit-targeted prompt injection or covert data transfer.

remediation.issue: The default run can send the full list to Leadsets without a separate approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Before any contact lookup, show the provider, fields, record count, estimated usage, and export destination. Require confirmation, send only necessary fields, and use a small default limit.

remediation.issue: Email verification is presented as clearance to send.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit verified status for Recovered. Remove sending recommendations for catch-all results, and require a suppression and permission check before any sending or campaign import.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk contact processing lacks a transfer approval step
semantic_findings.description: By default, the workflow rechecks all contacts and enriches unmatched records through Leadsets. It reports counts but does not require approval before submitting addresses or other identifiers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented default is all contacts. The workflow announces the count and estimates usage, then makes lookups without a separate transfer confirmation.

content.value_statement: A bounce report does not show which contacts have changed jobs or which original addresses still work. Bounce Recovery rechecks addresses with Leadsets and separates verified replacements from results that need review.
actual_capabilities: Normalize and deduplicate bounced addresses from a CSV, Sheet, CRM view, or sequencer export.
Check Leadsets usage and estimate records needed before processing.
Recheck original addresses and separate contacts whose original email now verifies.
Test one enrichment match, then compare returned companies and roles with the original list.
Export four result groups to CSV or Google Sheets and report group counts and records used.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and MCP or REST access. Verification and enrichment consume records.
Needs a full name and bounced email for each contact. Missing company or profile details can reduce match quality.
Catch-all and unknown results do not confirm deliverability. A verified address does not establish permission to contact someone.
Does not send email, restart campaigns, or manage your suppression list.

use_cases.title: Review bounces from a recent campaign
use_cases.description: Separate original addresses that now verify from contacts that need follow-up research.

use_cases.title: Prepare CRM contact updates
use_cases.description: Compare verified replacements with existing contact records in a separate export before approving changes.

use_cases.title: Plan a recovery run within quota
use_cases.description: Estimate Leadsets usage, test one match, and split a large list into batches that fit the available quota.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a bounce list
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Review a CSV before any external lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Count unique contacts in this bounce CSV and flag rows missing a name or email. Do not submit any records to Leadsets yet.

prompt_templates.title: Recheck original addresses
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: Test a small group of recent bounces.
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm, recheck the first 10 unique addresses with Leadsets. Report which originals now verify, and do not enrich any contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Find verified replacements
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Compare old and new contact details before updating a CRM.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the fields and estimated records for a 25-contact run. After approval, test one enrichment match, then export all four groups to CSV without changing the CRM.

prompt_templates.title: Run a quota-limited recovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Process an approved list across usage windows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Exclude contacts on my suppression list and propose batches within my Leadsets quota. Wait for approval before any lookup. Report usage, company changes, and unfinished rows in the Sheet I specify.

output_examples.input: Recheck 10 approved addresses and report the results without enrichment.
output_examples.output: Three original addresses now verify. Seven did not verify and remain unresolved because enrichment was skipped.

output_examples.input: Process this 30-contact batch and export the four result groups to a separate Sheet.
output: Still deliverable: 5 original addresses now verify.
Unresolved: 9 contacts without a verified replacement. No CRM records were changed.

best_practices: Approve the provider, destination, and maximum contact count before any lookups.
Test one enrichment match and confirm the person's identity before processing the rest.
Check consent and suppression lists before using any replacement address in a campaign.
anti_patterns: Submitting a full CRM export when the task requires only selected contacts and fields.
Treating a catch-all result or guessed address as verified.
Overwriting CRM fields before reviewing and approving the proposed changes.

faq.question: What information do I need to start?
faq.answer: Provide the full name and bounced email for each contact. A company, domain, title, or LinkedIn profile can help match the person.

faq.question: Where is my contact data processed?
faq.answer: Verification and enrichment send relevant contact data to Leadsets through its MCP server or REST API. Results go to the configured destination.

faq.question: Can I skip rechecking original addresses?
faq.answer: Yes. Skipping the recheck saves one enrichment record per original address, but it will not identify originals that now verify.

faq.question: How are verified and catch-all results different?
faq.answer: Recovered requires an explicit verified status for a new address. A catch-all domain accepts mail broadly, so the individual mailbox remains unconfirmed.

faq.question: What happens when the run reaches a usage limit?
faq.answer: The skill checks quota and plans batches. Rate limits can pause processing, and an exhausted free allowance stops the run.

faq.question: Will this update my CRM or restart outreach?
faq.answer: CRM or sequencer writeback requires your confirmation. The skill does not send messages, restart sequences, or remove suppressions.
